chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar and Burayd ibn Mu'awiyah, from one of the two of them عليه السلام, who said:

There is no objection to the praying person standing upon hair and wool, so long as he performs sajdah upon the earth. But if it is from the vegetation of the earth, then there is no objection to standing and performing sajdah upon it.

key_terms.نَبَاتِ ٱلْأَرْضِ: vegetation growing from the earth, suitable here for sajdah
key_terms.ٱلشَّعْرِ: hair used as a material beneath the worshipper
key_terms.ٱلصُّوفِ: wool used as a material beneath the worshipper
key_terms.ٱلْأَرْضِ: the earth/ground upon which sajdah is performed

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in salat to stand or perform sajdah on wool, hair, or plants from the earth?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about what may be beneath the worshipper during salat and what may be used for sajdah. It states that standing on hair or wool is permissible if sajdah is done on the earth, and that if the material is from the vegetation of the earth, both standing and sajdah upon it are permissible.
